key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 strongly tunes stability, bandgap, and solar-cell performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies composition control as a practical lever for designing more efficient perovskite-inspired absorbers for next-generation solar cells and optoelectronic devices.
method: Electronic band structure and bandgap analysis
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps from 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME efficiencies ranging from 0.6% for Ca3PF3 to 29.6% for Ca3PI3.
watch_item: The results are computational screening only, so experimental synthesis, stability under operating conditions, and device-level validation are still needed.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
